title: Irish crochet leaf motif
excerpt: A standalone leaf motif in fingering yarn using Irish crochet techniques. The raised surface is built on a padded foundation cord and surrounded by a picot edging.
sourceNotes: A basic Irish crochet leaf worked over a foundation cord with double crochets and trebles for the raised veins. Suitable as a first Irish crochet project.

glossaryTerms.definition: A length of yarn laid along the centre of an Irish crochet motif and worked over with tight double crochets. It raises the surface and gives firmness.
A decorative border of small loops, each formed by chaining 3 or 4 and slip-stitching into the first chain, worked at regular intervals along the edge of a motif.

crochet.gaugeText: Finished leaf approx. 6 cm long x 3 cm wide.
crochet.finishedSizeText: One leaf motif approx. 6 cm long.

Cut a 20 cm length of yarn for the padding cord. Fold it double and hold it along the centre of the work. Chain 14, then work double crochets tightly over both the chain and the padding cord on the way back to the start.

At the tip chain, work 3 dc into the tip to turn. Work dc along the second side of the foundation, covering the padding cord. At the base, work 2 trebles into the base stitch to form the leaf stalk. Pull the padding cord ends through to the back and secure.
Work around the outer edge: 2 dc then chain 3, slip stitch into 1st chain (picot), repeat every 3 stitches around. Fasten off and weave in the ends with the tapestry needle.
